what_happened: The the person running Athena did diagnosis work themselves. A flaky drain-stop test was failing. A job sent to find the cause could not reproduce it in two tries. The the person running Athena read main's GitHub CI run log, found the panic text that shows the race, and queued a new request that names the cause. This was an intervention, not a rejected job.
cause: Athena's isolated job had no access to CI run logs, which hold the evidence for intermittent failures, and could only try to reproduce the test locally. Nothing makes a flaky-test job start from the failure text on main, and nothing keeps the panic output of failed CI runs where Athena can read it. So root-cause diagnosis of an intermittent failure fell to the the person running Athena, who ended up supplying the method.
prevention: When a test fails intermittently on main or in CI, Athena should capture the failing run's panic and assertion text into a record in the repo or state directory, and attach it to any diagnosis job's request. A flaky-test job would then begin from the recorded failure, not from trying to reproduce it. Such a job should also be required to name the root cause, with evidence, before any fix is made. The whole class is a flaky failure diagnosed without its failure output.
proposed_request: Fix the flaky drain-stop test so it passes reliably. The race is shown in the panic text from main's CI run, which is pasted below. Before changing anything, name the root cause in the report and say which line of the test or code produces the race. Then fix that cause, not individual call sites. Show the fix works by running the drain-stop test repeatedly (for example 200 runs in a loop) with no failure. Change only the code and tests needed for this fix.
